description:
A settled reader runs once just to discover its input became unsettled. When a drain re-settles the cone above new work, every DeriveExecutableFacts in that cone is woken by the unsettling revision, runs, finds ActivationAnalyzed unsettled, blocks, and runs again after it settles: about two runs per executable per drain where one suffices.

Evidence (xxd10/a/p1.fz, quoted in fz-afu.13, on fz-xxd.10 revision 3 over 5ea6a5830): 13 quiescences, each re-settling 190-306 facts; ExecutableFacts 216 -> 664 runs against base; ExecutableFacts blocked on ActivationAnalyzed 312 times vs 86 at base; about 54 runs per drain over 28 executables. fz-afu.13 removes most of the drains here, which hides this cost but does not remove it.

Paper first: who subscribes a settled reader, and to which revisions; the reader should be woken by a settled revision of what it read, not by the unsettling one. Signal: runs per subject and wake causes for DeriveExecutableFacts in work_graph.applied. Close when each executable's facts run once per settled change of their inputs on p1 and on closure_capture_requirement_projection; no pin rises.
title: A settled reader runs only on a settled change, not to discover it became unsettled
